item.title: Trump to discuss leaving NATO in meeting with alliance’s leader, White House says
item.summary: The president, long a NATO skeptic, has been especially angry at alliance members in recent weeks for declining to take part in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

item.title: As Hegseth proclaims victory in Iran war, Caine takes cautious tone
item.summary: The defense secretary described the state of hostilities mostly in past tense. The Joint Chiefs chairman noted that the “ceasefire is a pause” in combat operations.

item.title: Israel kills dozens in Beirut, says Lebanon is not part of Iran truce
item.summary: Israeli strikes pounded the Lebanese capital, killing dozens of people in an aerial barrage hours after the U.S.-Iran ceasefire took hold.

item.title: Trump administration expected to slash Iran war funding request
item.summary: The eventual ask of Congress is likely to fall to between $80 billion and $100 billion, officials said, less than half the amount of an earlier proposal to offset costs of the conflict.

item.title: After pager attack on Hezbollah, Hungary offered help to Iran
item.summary: Revelations about a 2024 call offering assistance raise questions about Hungary’s ties to Iran as the Trump administration backs Prime Minister Viktor Orban for reelection.

item.title: Trump agrees to suspend attacks for two weeks if Iran opens Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: The president said he had received a 10-point proposal from Iran that formed a “workable basis” for negotiations. But Israel said the ceasefire “does not include Lebanon.”

item.title: Trump threats against civilian targets put military in legal, moral quandary
item.summary: President Donald Trump said the United States would target “every” Iranian bridge and power plant. Experts say such blanket action violates international law.

item.title: Pope Leo denounces Trump’s threat to destroy Iran’s ‘whole civilization’
item.summary: The Chicago-born pope suggested fellow Americans call their congressional representatives and ask for peace, not war.

item.title: JD Vance campaigns for far-right nationalist Viktor Orban in Hungary
item.summary: The vice president traveled to Budapest as Trump’s deadline for an Iran deal loomed Tuesday, backing the administration’s closest ideological ally in Europe.

item.title: Hegseth’s boastful claims about Iran war contradict reality, officials say
item.summary: The defense secretary’s rosy portrayal of U.S. success in the conflict risks misinforming the public and the president, observers worry.
